belief: People like us don't go to college.
origins: In some families, no one has gone to college, or college was something others did. Cost, fear of debt, a lack of information, a parent who feared losing a child to a different world, or a school that did not encourage it can all feed this belief. It can also be quiet: nobody forbade it, but nobody planned for it either. Many capable people never ask because they assume the door is not for them.
teaches: Scripture honors wisdom and learning in many forms: the craftsman, the farmer, the scholar, the shepherd, and the merchant. Proverbs says wisdom is supreme, so acquire wisdom, and the heart of the discerning acquires knowledge. James says that if any of us lacks wisdom, we may ask God, who gives generously without finding fault. Paul tells us to work at whatever we do with our whole being, for the Lord. College is not the only path, and it is not for everyone, but the belief that “people like us” cannot learn or train further is not from God.
self_statements: We cannot afford it, so there is no point looking.
If I go, I will not fit in.
It is better not to hope.
errors: Predicting that I would fail or not belong.
Treating my family’s history as a rule for me.
Ignoring evidence of my ability and effort.
Seeing college as the only path to learning or the only path I cannot take.
questions: Who in my family or community told me this, and what experiences were behind it?
What do I actually know about training options, costs, and aid?
What have I learned or mastered already that shows I can learn?
What kinds of training or schooling might fit my gifts?
What would I try if I knew I could handle it?
Who could I ask for information this month?
truth: God gives wisdom generously, and learning is open to people from every background. College may or may not be my path, but I can find out for myself instead of letting an old sentence decide. There are many good ways to grow, and I can take the next step with help.
hw_truths: I can ask God for wisdom.
Learning is for people like me, too.
My ability is not decided by my family’s history.
There are many paths to training and growth.
I can start with one conversation.
log: What I learned about my options
Each week, write one new fact you found about training, schooling, or funding.
actions: List skills and subjects you have mastered, in work, home, church, or school.
Visit a community college, trade program, or counselor and ask about costs and aid.
Talk with someone who has done it.
Ask a person from a similar background about their experience.
Tell your family what you are exploring so they can be part of it.
prayer: Father, You give wisdom to those who ask. Free me from the idea that learning is not for me. Show me the path that fits my gifts and give me courage to ask the first question. Amen.
hw_questions: Who told me college is not for me?
What do I actually know about my options?
What have I already learned to do well?
What would I try if I knew I could?
Who could I ask for information?
What is one question I can ask this month?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God gives wisdom generously, so I can ask about my next step in learning.”
